full_judgment:
Amin- Ur- Rahman Khan J.- By an application under section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code the petitioners obtained this rule to challenge the order dated 2 5.1985 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka rejecting an application submitted by the present petitioners as defendant Nos.1and 2 undo, section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Suit No. 314 of 1985. 

2. The Opposite parties numbering 26 filed Title Suit No. 211 of 1983 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge at Dhaka against 36 defendants including Dijendra Narayan Nandi who was defendant Na i for a declaration or their title in 3'71 lands of C S. plot Nets 76 and 94 and for a further declaration that decree dated 23 7 76 passed in Title Suit No. 25 of 19/5 of the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka is void The same opposite-p Jules subsequently brought Title Suit No 314 of 1985 against 34 principal defendants and 64 pro-defendants making the present petitioner defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in which they sought declaration of title in schedule 13-1 lands i e the entire land of C.S. p1or No.94 and part of C.S plot No 76 as also for declaration of title in the lands of schedule D-11 namely lands of plot Nos.92, 93. and 149 measuring P44, schedule E i.e., lands I. f C.S. plot No.141 with a further declaration that the decree dated 24 3.78 passed in Title Suit No 50 of 107e of first Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and mutation of the name of the defendant No.31 in S.A. Khatian No.178 on the basis of that decree was void 

3. The present petitioners being defendant Nos.1 and 2 in the subsequent suit, i e., Title Suit Vo.314 of 1985 made an application under section10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the proceeding of the subsequent Suit i.e, Suit  No. 314 of 1985 pending disposal of the earlier instituted suit namely, Title Suit No. 211/83, In their application the present Deletions submitted that though defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were not parties in the earlier instituted suit but Dijendra Narayan Nandi figured as defendant No, 1 in that suit and the present petitioners having claimed title on the basis of purchase from the Vendee of Dijendra Narayan Nandi who were parties in that suit and also since there was a common matter and commas) issue in respect of title over the lands of C.S, plot Nos. 76 and 94 involved in both the earlier instituted suit and the subsequently instituted suit, it was necessary according to the provision of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure to stay the proceedings of the later instituted suit until the disposal of the earlier suit while the parties and their successors were same Upon the said petition the plaintiff Opposite parries filed a written objection against the stay prayer upon the ground that most of the lands over which declaration of title was prayed for in the subsequent suit namely, title suit No 314 and many of the parties who were defendants in that suit were not the subject matter and parties in the earlier suit namely. Title Suit No. 211/83 and thus all the subject matter and all the facts in issue were not common in both the suits and so section 10 of the Civil Procedure Code was quite inapplicable and no stay could he granted as prayed for by the defendant Nos. t and 2 under the provision objection 10 of the Cede of Civil Procedure. 

4. The learned Subordinate Judge after considering the petition of the defendants and 2 and the objection of the plaintiffs and also after considering the provision of section 10 of the C P.C. gave his finding that the cause of action and matter in issue of the two suits are different arid upon such finding be rejected the prayer to; stay of tin suit.

5. Being aggrieved by that order the pre-sent Rule was obtained by the defendant Nos, 1 and 2 by an application under section ll5 of the Code of Civil Procedure 

6. Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submitted that the main matter in both the suit was the claim of title in C.S plot Nos. 94 and 76. As in the earlier Suit No 211/8 the declaration of title was sought only in respect of those 2(two) plots title while in the subsequent suit also the declaration of title was sought in respect of those two plots though declaration was also sought for in respect of some other plots in the subsequent suit. 

7 He further submitted that though pre-sent defendant' Nos r and 2 were not party in the former suit but still the defendant Nos. I and 2 claimed title through the persons who were parties in the former suit. In such a situation the provision of section 10 of the C P.0 was well applicable and according to the said provision the learned Subordinate Judge was required by law not to proceed with trial of the subsequent suit and consequently he should have granted the prayer under section 10 of the C P.C. In other words Mr Ishtiaq Mimed submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error of law in failing to exercise the jurisdiction vested in him by failing to stay the proceedings of the subsequent suit. 

8. On the other hand, Mr. Khondker Mahabubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite parties, submitted that except the prayer for declaration of tide in respect of C.S plot Nos. 94 and 76 which was the only issue that was common in both the suits all other mistress and issues of the subsequent suit were not at all concerned or involved in the earlier suit so when there were severs different issues involved in the subsequent suit which were not at all involved in the earlier suit the provision of section 10 of the C.P C was quite inapplicable. 

9. Section 10 of the Civil Procedure Code is in the following language t, "No Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter ID issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim litigation under the same title where such suit is pending in the same or any other Court In Bangladesh having jurisdiction to grant the relief claimed or in any Court beyond the Ironist of Bangladesh established or contained by the Government and having like jurisdiction, or before the Supreme Court". 

10. According the said provision, the matter in issue in the subsequently instituted suit must be directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit. This really means that the entire matter issue in both the suits must be same. Besides that the parties in both the suits should be the same or at least the parties must be such under whom they or any of them claim litigating under the same title ID this case all the matters in issue in the subsequent suit are not at all matters in issue in the former suit because in the subsequently instituted suit declaration of title has been claimed in respect of C S. plots No. 92, 93, 149, 56, 97 and 141 and none of these plots are subject-matter in the earlier instituted suit Similarly, in the earlier instituted suit there was the prayer for declaration that the decree in Title Suit No. 25/1975 was void and this matter is riot present at all in the subsequent suit. Again in the subsequently instituted suit declaration was sought in respect of a decree in Title Suit No. 50/1978 of the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka as being void and this matter was not till present in the earlier instituted suit. Further, regarding the parties, in the earlier suit only 36 persons were defendants while in the subsequent suit there were 34 defendants as also 6; pro-defendants, Thus it is found that all the matters in issue in the previously instituted suit were not matters in issue in the subsequent suit and also all the parties of the subsequently instituted suit were not parties in the earlier suit and thus most of the matters, issues and parties were different in the two suits. In fact out of several matters and issues only one matter and issue regarding the C.S. plot Nos. 76 and 94 were common in the two suits and every other matter and issue was different in the two suits. 

11. The expression "matter in issue" has referred to the entire subject controversy between the parties and the application for stay of suit under this section is bound to show that all the matters in issue in the suit are directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit. It is not sufficient that there are some issues common to the two suits but all the matters in issue in the two suits should be identical and Court cannot apply this section where there are some issues in common and also other different issues. Even when one of the issues in the two suits are common that is not sufficient to attract the operation of this section unless it could be shown that the entire subject in controversy was the same in both the suits. 

12. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed cited a decision in the case of Muhammad Younas Vs. Nargis Sultana, reported io PLD Lahore 1970, page 41 where also it has been held that every matter in dispute should be directly and substantially in issue in both suits and that one of several issues being common is insufficient for stay of subsequent suit. Another case has been referred to by Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed which is the case of Ch. Muhammad Afzal Vs. Mst. Sardar reported in PLO 1949 Lahore at page 16 wherein it has been held that section 10 of the C P.C. bars the trial of a suit when all the issues in both the suits are common and that the mere fact that one or two issues are common in the two suits is not sufficient for bringing the suit within the scope of section 10. The same being the accepted principle it is found that the present case cannot be held to be a case wherein section 10 of the C.P.C. can be applied. Thus it is found that the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any error of law in rejecting the defendant petitioner's prayer for stay and rather that was the only legal and proper order that could be passed. 

13. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submitted that in view of the fact that section 10 was not applicable and also in consideration of the fact that at least one issue was common in both the suits, so, he thought it to be most appropriate to seek an analogous hearing of both the suits and that an application for analogous hearing of the two suits has been already filed on behalf of the opposite parties before the learned Subordinate Judge which remains to be disposed of by him. Since the said petition is already before the learned Subordinate Judge for disposal we think it will not be proper to give our views in respect of the said petition. As he is competent to dispose of the same we refrain from making any comment in respect of the said prayer for analogous hearing and the said petition will be disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge in accordance with law In the result, the Rule is discharged with-out any order as to costs 

A.T.M. Afzal, J.—I agree. 
End.
